resolver_rules.rule: Serve when owner-approved and eligible for runtime bundle.
Serve only when full article is unavailable. Never compose from generic adjective vocab.
Serve rather than synthesizing unreviewed prose.
Latitude > 0 north, latitude < 0 south, unknown/equatorial neutral.
Render all relevant active supported aspects; do not arbitrarily choose one.

resolver_rules.key_or_source: sign-specific retrograde first, then planet-level fallback
resolver_rules.rule: Retrograde is a modifier to the base article, not a replacement intro.

metadata_contract.note: Use first ingress date of the occurrence/cycle, including retrograde re-entries.
Use TLDR everywhere reader-facing. Do not use TL;DR.

metadata_contract.value: Hellenistic, whole-sign houses, traditional rulership primary
metadata_contract.note: Modern Aquarius/Uranus, Pisces/Neptune, Scorpio/Pluto associations allowed editorially but not as structural ruler substitutions.
Do not write 'tropical zodiac year' in reader copy.

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Aries begins the zodiac year and brings attention to initiative, courage, boundaries, and the choices that set something in motion.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: A beginning becomes real when you give it direction.
sun_articles.opening: Aries is the spark that sets the wheel of the zodiac into motion. What are you ready to begin? What do you want badly enough to stop waiting for the perfect moment?
sun_articles.tension: Aries moves quickly, and speed can feel like certainty when you are tired of waiting. The useful distinction is between a first move that gives you new information and an impulse that only gets you out of the discomfort of not knowing. Courage is not the same as urgency.
sun_articles.development: This is a season to notice where you have been waiting for permission, agreement, or confidence before acting on something you already care about. Action creates feedback. A boundary changes the terms. A decision creates a direction. Once something is moving, you have something concrete to respond to instead of another imagined outcome.
sun_articles.close: Choose the move that makes the decision real. You can learn from what happens next.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: Aries is the spark that sets the wheel of the zodiac into motion.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: You may already know what you want to begin but keep waiting for permission, agreement, or confidence before you make it real.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Choose the move that gives you something concrete to respond to.

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Taurus turns attention toward value, resources, and what you are willing to sustain over time.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: If you want something to grow, it has to receive more than good intentions.
sun_articles.opening: The Sun enters Taurus, and your values become harder to separate from the way you spend your resources. What gets your time, money, attention, and care is what you are actively building, regardless of what you say matters to you. This month is a chance to put more behind the people, skills, work, and parts of your life you actually want to grow.
sun_articles.tension: Taurus can reveal how much of your life is being funded by habit. Something can be familiar, expensive, or years in the making and still no longer deserve the same share of your resources. Keeping what you have and investing in what you want are not always the same decision.
sun_articles.development: Look at what your calendar, budget, attention, and care are already supporting. That is where your priorities become material. This is not about turning every choice into a calculation. It is about noticing where your resources keep flowing by default and deciding which people, skills, work, relationships, and parts of your life you still want to develop.
sun_articles.close: Put more behind what you want to keep growing.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: The Sun in Taurus makes your values visible through where your resources go.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: Your calendar, budget, attention, and care show what you are actively supporting, even when your stated priorities say something else.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Put more behind what you want to keep growing.

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Gemini brings movement to conversation, learning, language, and the choices you make with information.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: You do not need more information when the issue is that you are avoiding what you already know.
sun_articles.opening: Gemini Season begins on {{entryDate}}, inviting a shift toward movement, conversation, learning, and conscious curiosity. This is a time to notice what you’re saying, what you avoid, and why. Words are choices that reveal alignment or avoidance.
sun_articles.tension: Gemini can keep the mind moving long after movement stops being useful. Another source, another opinion, another conversation, another possible explanation can feel productive while making it easier not to decide. Curiosity becomes avoidance when every new piece of information gives you another reason to postpone your own conclusion.
sun_articles.development: Use the season to question what you were taught, what you keep repeating, and what you assume is true because it is familiar. Who taught you that? Is it still true? The point is not to distrust everything. It is to become more conscious of what you let shape your thinking, whose language you are borrowing, and which questions actually help you understand something better. Information is everywhere. Discernment is what makes it useful.
sun_articles.close: Ask the better question. Then notice which answer changes what you do.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: Gemini Season shifts attention toward movement, conversation, learning, and conscious curiosity.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: Another source or opinion can help, but it can also become a reason to postpone a conclusion you already know how to make.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Ask the better question, then notice which answer changes what you do.

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Cancer brings home, family, care, memory, and emotional safety into focus.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: You can keep pushing without support, but you will pay for it somewhere.
sun_articles.opening: Cancer Season is a chance to come home to yourself. Tell yourself the truth about what feels supportive and what does not. Your body, your home, and your closest relationships affect how much of you is available for everything else.
sun_articles.tension: Care can become automatic with the people you love. You remember, adjust, protect, make room, and keep going because someone has to. The problem begins when being dependable means your needs are always the first ones postponed, or when support only moves in one direction.
sun_articles.development: Cancer brings the foundation into view. What helps you feel safe enough to rest, speak honestly, take a risk, or ask for help? Which family patterns still shape your choices even though the circumstances have changed? You do not need to blame anyone to notice what keeps repeating. You can start with where you are now and strengthen what actually supports you.
sun_articles.close: The strongest growth begins at the roots.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: Cancer Season brings the foundation back into view.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: Your body, home, and closest relationships affect how much of you is available for everything else.
sun_articles.source_notes: Source concepts: shift from doing to feeling; home/family/emotional safety; care; support; foundation; repeated family patterns. Close preserves owner phrase 'The strongest growth begins at the roots.'

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Leo brings creativity, love, desire, play, pride, and visibility into focus.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: Being seen is not the same as being understood, loved, or valued.
sun_articles.opening: As Cancer Season gives way to Leo, a new self begins to take shape, one rooted in safety and revealed through joy. We are not escaping our vulnerability; we are creating from it. The question becomes what you are willing to show once you no longer need to hide every tender part of yourself.
sun_articles.tension: Leo wants expression, but visibility can pull attention toward reaction. A creative block, a quiet response, or being overlooked can suddenly feel like evidence that the work or desire itself does not matter. Recognition can feel good. It becomes a problem when other people’s response gets to decide what you are allowed to love.
sun_articles.development: This season brings you back to what makes you feel alive enough to participate fully. Creativity, romance, humor, play, and self-expression are not distractions from a serious life. They are part of how you discover what matters enough to put your heart behind it. Notice who sees you, who celebrates you, and where you still change yourself to avoid ridicule or rejection.
sun_articles.close: Create from the part of you that feels alive, not the part waiting to be approved.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: Leo Season brings visibility, creativity, love, and desire into focus.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: You can want recognition and still notice when other people’s response starts deciding what you are allowed to love.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Create from the part of you that feels alive, not the part waiting to be approved.

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Virgo brings attention to routines, work, health, systems, and the details that keep daily life functioning.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: A system is only useful if it makes your life more workable.
sun_articles.opening: Virgo Season is a reality check. This is the month to recognize which systems actually support you and which ones are daily punishment disguised as productivity. The point is not to organize everything. It is to notice what keeps creating more work.
sun_articles.tension: Virgo can become so focused on improvement that the process itself turns into another source of pressure. You can track every habit, refine every plan, and keep fixing things that were never the problem. Attention to detail is useful when it changes the outcome. It is exhausting when every detail gets treated like an emergency.
sun_articles.development: Look at the routines and responsibilities that repeat. Where does one small problem keep creating three more tasks? What work is invisible because it only gets noticed when it stops? This is the season to repair the system, clarify the responsibility, or remove the step that keeps wasting time. The details matter, but not all equally.
sun_articles.close: Fix what keeps creating more work, then leave the rest alone.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: Virgo Season is a reality check.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: A routine can look disciplined and still make your life harder every day.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Fix what keeps creating more work.
sun_articles.source_notes: Source concepts: reality check; systems that support versus punish; invisible work; details; productivity; perfectionism. Opening preserves owner phrase 'reality check' and 'daily punishment disguised as productivity.'

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Libra brings relationships, agreements, fairness, and the balance between your needs and someone else’s into focus.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: Keeping the peace is not balance if one person is doing all the adjusting.
sun_articles.opening: Balance is a moment, not a state. It is a pause in constant motion, not a destination you arrive at. Libra Season makes that easier to see in relationships, where every agreement depends on what each person is actually giving, receiving, changing, and carrying.
sun_articles.tension: Harmony can hide a lot. A relationship can look peaceful because one person keeps swallowing the disagreement, moving the deadline, changing the plan, or doing the emotional work for both people. The absence of conflict does not tell you that the arrangement is fair.
sun_articles.development: This season brings the exchange into focus. Who gets heard? Who keeps adjusting? Who benefits when nothing changes? Some conflicts are worth having because they reveal what the relationship can actually hold. Honest compromise comes from choice. Self-abandonment happens when keeping the connection requires you to disappear inside it.
sun_articles.close: This season teaches you the difference between keeping the peace and creating it.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: Balance is a moment, not a state.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: A peaceful arrangement can still depend on one person doing all the adjusting.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Look at what each person is actually carrying.
sun_articles.source_notes: Source concepts: balance is movement; honest assessment of who carries weight; relationship exchange; honest compromise versus self-abandonment; keeping peace versus creating it. Opening and close preserve owner phrases.

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Scorpio brings attention to endings, intimacy, shared resources, power, and what has been kept below the surface.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: Transformation gets harder when you keep spending energy on something that has already ended.
sun_articles.opening: The Sun enters Scorpio, and what is already over becomes harder to keep propping up. Scorpio does not kill what is alive. It names what is already dead and makes you look at why you are still carrying it.
sun_articles.tension: The difficult part is that endings are rarely clean. A relationship can be over emotionally before the logistics change. A role can stop fitting before you know what comes next. A financial or emotional agreement can keep operating long after it stopped being fair. Control can make the old arrangement feel safer than the unknown, even while it drains you.
sun_articles.development: Scorpio brings attention to what is shared, hidden, owed, feared, desired, and difficult to admit. This is where power dynamics become easier to see. It is also where you find out what becomes available when you stop protecting an arrangement simply because you know how to survive inside it. Transformation is not the breakdown. Refusing it can be.
sun_articles.close: Name what has ended so your energy can stop keeping it alive.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: The Sun enters Scorpio, and what is already over becomes harder to keep propping up.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: An old arrangement can keep running long after it stopped being fair, useful, or alive.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Stop spending energy keeping an ending on life support.
sun_articles.source_notes: Source concepts: Scorpio names what is already dead; composting; transformation; shared resources; power; control; endings that happened emotionally before logistics caught up. Opening closely follows owner wording.

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Sagittarius brings beliefs, meaning, direction, perspective, and the story you are living by into focus.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: A belief is only useful if your life can still support it.
sun_articles.opening: Sagittarius Season brings the story you are living by into focus. What do you still claim to believe, and does your life reflect that belief? The answer can change your direction.
sun_articles.tension: Sagittarius looks for the larger meaning, but a bigger story can become another way to skip over facts that do not fit it. Optimism can keep you moving, but it can also keep you loyal to a plan, relationship, or worldview long after the evidence has changed. The point is not to lose faith. It is to know what your faith is built on.
sun_articles.development: This is a season for widening the frame. Travel, study, teaching, philosophy, religion, publishing, and unfamiliar perspectives can all challenge the story you have been using to explain your life. Gemini collects the information. Sagittarius decides what it means. That meaning matters because beliefs become choices, and choices become direction.
sun_articles.close: Choose the story you are willing to build a life around.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: Sagittarius Season brings the story you are living by into focus.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: A belief can guide you for years and still stop matching the life you are actually living.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Choose the story you are willing to build a life around.

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Capricorn brings responsibility, time, authority, ambition, and the structures that support long-term goals into focus.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: Doubt can be useful when it shows you what still needs a plan.
sun_articles.opening: Capricorn Season is where the plan has to answer to time, responsibility, and what you are actually willing to do. Maturity means confronting the truth of where you stand, not only where you intended to be. A goal becomes different once you can see the work, cost, and consequences attached to it.
sun_articles.tension: Ambition can keep you moving through conditions that should have been reconsidered months ago. Responsibility can also collect around the person who has proved they will carry it. The problem is not wanting too much. It is building a version of success that only works because you are always the one absorbing the pressure.
sun_articles.development: Saturn rules Capricorn, which is why time matters here. Deadlines, limits, hierarchy, commitments, reputation, and long-range consequences all make the plan more concrete. Doubt does not automatically mean stop. Sometimes it points to the weak part of the structure, the missing resource, or the responsibility that needs to be redistributed before you keep climbing.
sun_articles.close: Build something that can support your life after the achievement.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: Capricorn Season brings the plan into contact with time, responsibility, and consequence.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: A goal changes once you can see who is carrying the work, what it costs, and what has to happen next.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Use doubt to find the weak part of the plan.
sun_articles.source_notes: Source concepts: accountability; pragmatism; maturity through responsibility; doubt as information; time; long-term goals; legacy; practical steps.

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Aquarius brings community, systems, ideas, individuality, and the future you are helping create into focus.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: Your difference matters most when it changes what becomes possible for more than one person.
sun_articles.opening: The Sun in Aquarius illuminates the space between what has been and what could be. This is the season to get clear about who you stand with and what you stand for. The future stops being an abstract idea once your values start changing how you participate in the present.
sun_articles.tension: Aquarius can see the system clearly enough to critique it, but seeing the flaw is not the same as building something better. Distance can protect independent thought, yet too much distance can leave you describing the problem while other people are still living with it.
sun_articles.development: Aquarius is traditionally ruled by Saturn, which gives the sign its relationship to systems, structures, responsibility, and the rules groups live by. Its modern association with Uranus adds the language of disruption, experimentation, and change. Those ideas become most useful when innovation has somewhere to go: a community, a tool, a policy, a network, or a different way of organizing people and resources.
sun_articles.close: Build the future in a way other people can actually use.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: The Sun in Aquarius illuminates the space between what has been and what could be.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: Seeing what is wrong with a system matters less if nothing changes for the people still living with it.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Turn the idea into something people can use.

sun_articles.tldr_what: The Sun in Pisces brings endings, intuition, imagination, grief, surrender, and the unfinished parts of the current cycle into focus.
sun_articles.tldr_takeaway: Not every ending needs a clean explanation before you let it be over.
sun_articles.opening: Pisces is the last sign of the zodiac. This is the threshold between the past and the future, when old dreams, unfinished feelings, and stories you thought you had moved past can return for one more look. This is the final tide before Aries Season.
sun_articles.tension: Pisces can make longing feel meaningful enough to follow even when the facts are thin. Intuition matters here, but so does the distinction between what you sense and what you want to be true. Surrender is not the same as giving up, and imagination is not a substitute for evidence.
sun_articles.development: Traditionally ruled by Jupiter and associated with Neptune in modern astrology, Pisces reaches beyond what can be easily measured or explained. Dreams, symbols, grief, art, faith, memory, and uncertainty can all carry information, but they do not always arrive as instructions. This is a season for letting something finish, allowing an old story to lose its grip, and making space before the zodiac begins again.
sun_articles.close: Let the ending finish. Aries will bring movement soon enough.
sun_articles.fallback_hook: Pisces is the last sign of the zodiac.
sun_articles.fallback_lived: Old dreams, grief, unfinished feelings, and stories you thought you were done with can return before the cycle closes.
sun_articles.fallback_turn: Let the ending finish before you decide what comes next.

seasonal_contexts.copy: At the March equinox, day and night are nearly equal before the Northern Hemisphere begins tipping toward more light. Aries Season begins at the same moment, opening the zodiac year with a visible shift toward growth, motion, and longer days.

At the March equinox, day and night are nearly equal before the Southern Hemisphere begins tipping toward longer nights. Aries Season still begins the zodiac year. The season changes direction while the astrology turns toward initiation, choice, and what begins now.
The Sun enters Aries at the March equinox, when day and night are nearly equal across the globe. It is one of the four turning points of the solar year and the beginning of the zodiac year.

The June solstice marks the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, a turning point where light peaks, then slowly begins its descent. The Sun enters Cancer at the same moment, bringing the focus back to home, care, and what supports you from the inside.

The June solstice marks the shortest day of the year in the Southern Hemisphere, a turning point where darkness peaks and the light slowly begins to return. The Sun enters Cancer at the same moment, bringing the focus back to home, care, and what supports you from the inside.
The Sun enters Cancer at the June solstice, one of the four turning points of the solar year. Across the globe, the balance of light changes direction at the same moment Cancer Season begins.

At the September equinox, day and night are equal for approximately one moment. Then darkness begins to overtake light in the Northern Hemisphere. Balance is a moment, not a state. Libra Season begins at that turning point, bringing relationships, fairness, and the exchange between people into focus.

At the September equinox, day and night are equal for approximately one moment. Then light begins to overtake darkness in the Southern Hemisphere. Balance is a moment, not a state. Libra Season begins at that turning point, bringing relationships, fairness, and the exchange between people into focus.

At the September equinox, day and night meet at a point of near-equality before the balance shifts again. Libra Season begins at that turning point, a reminder that balance requires ongoing adjustment.

The December solstice marks the darkest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. From here, the light slowly begins to return. Capricorn Season begins at the same turning point, bringing time, responsibility, and what you are building for the long term into focus.

The December solstice marks the longest day of the year in the Southern Hemisphere. From here, the light slowly begins to recede. Capricorn Season begins at the same turning point, bringing time, responsibility, and what you are building for the long term into focus.

The Sun enters Capricorn at the December solstice, one of the four turning points of the solar year. The balance of light changes direction as Capricorn Season brings time, responsibility, and long-range consequences into focus.
